issues.title: KFF Cannot be added as an inferred dependency
issues.body: Because kotlinforforge doesn't contain a proper neoforge.mods.toml in the expected place, it doesn't get an id assigned by mod platforms and thus cannot be added as a dependency via tools like mcpublish. There should be a neoforge.mods.toml here below (the one you have in kffmod/) Example from my mod: The fact that this file is missing causes platforms like modrinth and curseforge to not be able to pull the id automatically, making it impossible for services like mcpublish to mark the dependency when publishing the mod. I think the best way to implement this would be to update your gradle script to drop a copy of the kffmod toml in META-INF. Hope this makes sense, thanks!

issues.title: KFF registers @EventBusSubscriber multiple times if multiple @Mod annotation in mod exists
issues.body:
There can be multiple `@Mod` annotated class in one mod, for example Create mod has two([Create](https://github.com/Creators-of-Create/Create/blob/d943a866c5b24f79a94427dff4deb3b99261f15c/src/main/java/com/simibubi/create/Create.java#L66), [CreateClient](https://github.com/Creators-of-Create/Create/blob/d943a866c5b24f79a94427dff4deb3b99261f15c/src/main/java/com/simibubi/create/CreateClient.java#L51)) `@Mod class`.
If KFF is to support same semantics as JavaModLoader, it should support this case. However, kfflang-neoforge seems to run `AutoKotlinEventBusSubscriber.inject` as many times as `@Mod` class exists in one mod.

See the code differences between [kfflang](https://github.com/thedarkcolour/KotlinForForge/blob/105380d7f505d14872fc9f6fb8453be18610dfef/src/kfflang/neoforge/kotlin/thedarkcolour/kotlinforforge/neoforge/KotlinModContainer.kt#L125) and [JavaModLoader](https://github.com/neoforged/FancyModLoader/blob/58a1eccc7d51431b907a83559adea14c4adac57b/loader/src/main/java/net/neoforged/fml/javafmlmod/FMLModContainer.java#L127).

issues.body:
Referencing https://github.com/fzzyhmstrs/fconfig/issues/102. 

KFF runs fine in dev environment (`runClient` etc) on it's own, but when another kotlin mod is added (Fzzy Config, which wants it as a runtime dep), it crashes with the linked error (also linked below)

[https://mclo.gs/cnGQ0XP](https://mclo.gs/cnGQ0XP)

Many combinations of `exclude`ing various bits and bobs have been attempted without success. There is a comment in KFF source that mentions `// ? to avoid classloading kotlin Intrinsics`. That appears to not be working, or there is another layer of issue interfering with that solution. Or it works for KFF in the version method, but when actually trying to load another mod using `loadMod`, the issue is encountered again.

I'm not entirely sure what the fix is in the "to avoid classloading" bit, but my guess is loading via `javaClass` instead of `.class::java`? In that case the issue may be related to the `KotlinModContainer`, which does still use `::class.java`

issues.title: [1.21.1-Neoforge] EventBusSubscriber Annotation doesn't work on Java class
issues.body:
I want to integrate KFF into a large codebase incrementally. I was happy to see that the `@Mod` annotation works for my main Java mod class, even when using KFF loader. 

I expected the `@EventBusSubscriber` annotation to do the same on my events class (uses **static** methods), but it doesn't. It doesn't even complain, Neo just crashes because of unregistered stuff. Switching my event class to Kotlin object immediately solved it.

I don't know how KFF works, so I dont know if this is feasible, but it should definitely be documented somewhere. I spent hours debugging it, since there is no visible KFF error. The skeleton projects have no dedicated event file example.

To be clear, the issue is: Following the steps in README for an existing mod, the resulting setup may sometimes crash, due to events not being loaded.

issues.title: [Feature Request] Update to kotlin 1.5.0?
Suggestion: Consider a more permissive license than GPL-3.0
issues.body:
I would like to bring up, once again, the discussion from #5, especially my ( I believe ) unnoticed reply https://github.com/thedarkcolour/KotlinForForge/issues/5#issuecomment-764461698 

My suggestion is to use a permissive license, such as LGPL 2.1/3 or even MIT/Apache/BSD/... in order to give modders the freedom to choose their own license for their creations if they use your library.

Why do I make this suggestion? Well, personally I like to license my mods under very permissive licenses such as the MIT, in order to allow people to freely use it for their projects, without having to worry about licenses too much. At the same time I'd like to use your work in a future project, to make my own life easier, but without restricting the freedom of those that want to base their works on my (future) work :) 

Currently your library is under GPL-3.0, which means that anyone who wants to use it needs to license their own mod under GPL-3.0 as well, they **cannot** choose their own license. Compared to that forge uses the more liberal LGPL, that allows modders to choose a license for their own work freely.

Based on your reply https://github.com/thedarkcolour/KotlinForForge/issues/5#issuecomment-698544319 I believe you actually want the same thing that forge wants: Giving modders freedom, which in turn allows more people to use your library compliantly.

If that is not the case and you chose GPL-3.0 deliberately to make sure people share their own mods under the GPL-3.0, then please ignore this issue. 

Finally, thank you for the great work you did with this library, and if I can help clear up any licensing questions feel free to ask!
